So, One Piece is the most successful manga of all time (or comic, apparently, according to the new record)

Now as a One Piece reader the reason for that seems painfully obvious to me -- I mean, it's awesome.

But it got me wondering, why exactly is One Piece so freakishly popular? It's been said that in Japan, even people who don't care about manga at all love One Piece.

It's so extraordinarily more popular than everything else, and my question is... why? What is it about One Piece that makes people love it so much?
Let's start a discussion! Something we can all talk about: What do you love about One Piece?

For me it is the balance of everything and Oda's inclusion of History and Pop culture into this unique universe. Lore and mythos are a powerful tool in OP. Everything seems to adhere strictly to the laws of the OP universe. As someone who doesn't enjoy much fiction this is the most important point. When a rule has been established Oda sticks to it (water vs devil fruits). The world itself is interesting with North, South, East, and West Blue; the Grand Line; and the New World. Then you have tools like the Log Pose to help you navigate. The level of intricate detail adds to the believability.

Haki Devil Fruit Ancient Weapons
Kenbunshoku Zoan Poseidon
Busoshoku Paramecia Pluton
Haoshoku Logia Uranus

Certain fruits seem stronger than others and at first we were lead to believe that someone made of sand, lava, or light would be invincible. But Haki is there to help balance it out so that no one person could be immune to damage.

Then we have the structure of the world

Pirates Marines Revolutionaries
Pirate King Gorosei Dragon
4 Yonko Commander-in-Chief Commander (Ivankov)
Supernovas/Shichibukai 3 Admirals & Cipher Pol Cheif of Staff

I think all of those points are things one would appreciate after really getting into One Piece, but I don't think they're responsible for the fact that One Piece has so many casual fans. Y'know what I mean?
I do know what you mean, but that was what kept me around. If it hadn't had this kind of structure I would have lost interest.

What do I like best about One Piece?

It's probably the worldbuilding and the sense of adventure the series has. When reading the manga, I prefer the buildup and epilogue of arcs over the fighting, just because every island is unique and I can't wait for the reveals that happen, the characters that are introduced and of course the Straw Hat Crew, how they interact with each other and how they navigate through the One Piece world.

I also really like the obscure references to history, real world pirates, little details that let people make ridiculous or amazing theories that sometimes end up being true.

The ideals expressed in the show. The pursuit of absolute freedom. It just gets to me. The feeling, the only was I can describe it, is like wind passing through me. It sounds silly but whatever its why I love the series.
It's not silly at all. I really get what you mean, this is what One Piece feels like. The way you feel as a child exploring something, an adventure, the wind that engulfs you. That's One Piece.

I love how the world and rules are revealed as they become more relevant, and how Oda isn't afraid to change how the world is "balanced" every couple hundred chapters, by introducing a new move or mechanic. Its almost a miracle how he can do that and manage to not turn Luffy into a Mary Sue. Now, almost 800 chapters later, things are balanced that nobody even thought about half the story ago.

I also really enjoy how Oda plays with the number three. Three types of Haki, the monster trio, three main factions, ASL, three types of DF, I could go on and on.

Its also nice that you can tell Oda isnt making this up as he does along. He has had a grand plan since the beginning. He'll leave Easter eggs in the story that we wont get until a couple hundred chapters later. Furthermore, the world feels dynamic because we find seemingly minor characters early on, and multiple arcs later they are relevant again, such as Bellamy or Mr3.

There is also quite a lot of meaning that isnt immediately obvious.
